title: Rethinking Sequential Locate-Then-Edit: Optimality and Stability
abstract: arXiv:2611.33692v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The Locate-Then-Edit framework enables efficient knowledge updates in large language models without requiring full retraining. Recent research has increasingly focused on sequential editing, where knowledge arrives continuously and the model is updated incrementally. However, existing sequential methods commonly suffer from catastrophic forgetting and model collapse after only a few hundred edits. In contrast, batch editing - which jointly optimizes all edits and yields the optimal solution under a specified editing objective - can support tens of thousands of edits with high edit efficacy while preserving the model's general capabilities, resulting in a substantial performance gap between the two editing paradigms. In this paper, we demonstrate that this gap can be closed via a batch-equivalent sequential editing approach. translated_title: 重新思考顺序式定位后编辑：最优性与稳定性
translated_abstract: 定位后编辑框架能够在无需完整重新训练的情况下，实现对大语言模型的高效知识更新。近期研究日益聚焦于顺序编辑，即知识持续到来、模型被逐步增量更新。然而，现有的顺序编辑方法通常在仅进行几百次编辑后就会出现灾难性遗忘和模型崩溃。相比之下，批量编辑——即联合优化所有编辑并在指定编辑目标下取得最优解——可以在保持模型通用能力的同时，支持数万次编辑并维持较高的编辑效能，这导致两种编辑范式之间存在显著的性能差距。在本文中，我们证明了这一差距可以通过一种与批量编辑等价的顺序编辑方法来弥合。此外，我们还通过分析揭示了现有顺序方法中模型退化的内在机制。
tldr: 本文提出一种与批量编辑等价的顺序编辑方法，成功弥合了顺序编辑与批量编辑之间的性能差距，解决了现有顺序方法在数百次编辑后出现的灾难性遗忘和模型崩溃问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a batch-equivalent sequential editing approach that closes the performance gap between sequential and batch editing, addressing the catastrophic forgetting and model collapse suffered by existing sequential methods after only a few hundred edits.
